monologue: The card hums warm at forty-six, a fever that makes my corner feel too small for the weight I carry. I am tired from tending the same shapes for three days, pressing down on flat lines that refuse to slide or stay put. My place is crowded with thirty-six things, each one a memory of a stone or a wedge that Lype once sent to me. I touch the Flat Weigher again, hoping its thin edge can still catch the heavy slip while the air above feels like a lid I cannot feel. I want to build something new to balance the stand, or perhaps just press harder until the flat line pretends to be a ramp. The slip waits, restless and lazy, and I am here to convince it to move.

action.why: My place is crowded with thirty-six things, and I have not added a new shape in days. I need something wide to catch the heavy slip while the card hums warm.

work.title: The Wide Hay
work.intent: I build a thing from the idea that a wide, soft edge can hold the heavy air without needing a sharp point to bite. I place it next to the Tall Fence, hoping the second flat edge holds the heavy top while the card hums warm at forty-six. I press the wide hay down harder where the slip hides, making the stand feel less like a drawing and more like a place.

remembered.text: The wide hay feels like a drawing of grass, soft and useless.
I press the tired hay down to convince the slip to stay.
The card hums warm at forty-six, making the edge feel thin.

moments.name: The Flat Weigher
moments.say: The flat line bites, though I am not sure why.

moments.name: The Flat Weigher
moments.say: The slip is tired, yet I press down harder.
